item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00501","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C19","C23","C03"],"selected_candidate_label":"C19","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C19 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child’s treatment of Summit preparations. Both letters reject a Soviet attempt to privilege its own agenda and exclude Western subjects, insist that neither side should possess a veto over topics, and propose preparatory work through ambassadors or foreign ministers to determine whether a productive Heads-of-Government meeting is possible. C23 contains an earlier version of the same preparatory machinery, while C03 supplies only the more general condition that a summit should promise significant results.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Western Governments cannot agree that the discussions ... should be based exclusively on the Soviet list any more than they would expect the Soviet Government to agree to base the discussions solely on the Western list","parent_excerpt":"I wrote that ... I would be willing to discuss your proposals in good faith if you would so discuss mine. Your answer is that I must be prepared to discuss your proposals ... In other words, you demand the right to veto discussion of the matters I believe to be vital to peace.","explanation":"Both use the same reciprocal-agenda argument to reject Soviet control over which subjects may be discussed."},{"child_excerpt":"Neither side would, during the preparatory stage, have been able to veto the inclusion of any topic for discussion","parent_excerpt":"you demand the right to veto discussion of the matters I believe to be vital to peace","explanation":"The child converts C19’s distinctive veto objection into an explicit rule for the preparatory procedure."},{"child_excerpt":"the Soviet foreign Minister and the Ambassadors could have proceeded to examine the positions of the various governments ... and establish what subjects should be submitted for examination by the Heads of Government","parent_excerpt":"Exchanges of views effected through our Ambassadors or Foreign Ministers may serve better ... exploring, through more normal channels, the prospects of a top-level meeting which would be adequate as to subjects","explanation":"This is substantially the same diplomatic machinery and sequence: ambassadorial or foreign-minister preparation, examination of subjects, then a possible summit."}]}
